parts.latex: Which data collected about a virus could be classified as both categorical and nominal?

solutions.latex:
Categorical data is sorted into categories rather than measured or counted; nominal categories have no natural order.

The country where the virus originated is a name with no order, so it is categorical and nominal.

The number of people, the rate of spread and the length of time are all numerical, so they are not categorical (options A, C, D).

$$\therefore\ \text{the country the virus originated (option B)}$$

parts.latex: Which set of data is classified as categorical and nominal?

solutions.latex:
Categorical data is sorted into categories rather than measured. Nominal categorical data has no natural order.

Colours (blue, red, black) are categories with no order, so they are categorical and nominal.

Cup size has an order (ordinal). Heights and numbers of students are numerical.

Hence the answer is option A.
